attacks.claim: The unpublish control is a <span> with an onClick handler. It is not focusable, has no role, and has no keyboard activation. Its icon is aria-hidden and there is no accessible name. Keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot unpublish from the queue, which violates WCAG 2.1 AA (2.1.1, 4.1.2).

The embargo badge hardcodes white text. In the light theme the surface is #ffffff, so the text is white on white and invisible (contrast about 1:1, WCAG 1.4.3). The embargo state, the PR's main value, is unreadable in the default theme.

The badge renders as invisible text in the default light theme, leaving only an empty amber outline pill. This is a visible rendering bug in the default theme, and it ignores the theme tokens that the app uses elsewhere.
The embargo badge is conveyed only by an amber outline and text. The hover state on the unpublish control is color-only, and no focus style is defined for it.

The row's visible text is not tied to the confirm dialog. A headline containing quotes or markup is interpolated into the dialog body. This is fine if confirm renders text, but nothing here guarantees that.
attacks.evidence: body: `"${draft.headline}" will be removed from the site...`

attacks.claim: onUnpublish rejection is not handled. A failed unpublish gives the editor no feedback, and the failure surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection. For a story that went out early, this makes a silent failure costly.
